Mixed-Reality Simulation With Preservice Teacher Candidates: A Conceptual Replication
Walters, Sharon M.; Hirsch, Shanna E.; McKown, Georgia; Carlson, Alex; Allen, Abigail A.
DOI: 10.1177/08884064211001453

Abstract
Given the critical importance of discrete instructional practices in special education, teacher candidates must be prepared to implement them upon entering the classroom. In preservice teacher education programs, field placements and clinical experiences rarely provide enough opportunities for preservice teachers to gain the proficiency needed to provide effective instruction. In this study, a randomized control research design was used to investigate the effects of a mixed-reality simulation experience compared with traditional classroom practice in the implementation of a system of least prompts. Results suggest that mixed-reality simulation with additional coaching supports significantly improved preservice teachers’ implementation of the prompting sequence. decisions.reason: The complete deposited references include one positively matching empirical finding: VinceGarland etal individual clinical coaching in TLETeachLivE improves novice teachers system-of-least-prompts implementation fidelity. Its primary original abstract reports six novice educators and this specific training/skill result; the current conceptual-replication title and abstract test coached mixed-reality SLPimplementation against classroom practice. Other simulation/teacher-education/reading-comprehension/bullying references do not positively report that same joint SLPcoaching/fidelity finding. Step2 permits naming this unique entry by description without an explicit in-text citation in the available abstract. Bind existing145, preserving verified2015online/2016print identity as one work. No full protocol equivalence, exact replication, hidden current comparisons or outcome is inferred.

decisions.reason: Prior state and expert files are absent; prior adjudication returned undeterminable before reference and original-source recovery. The current source (0091161cad153f3e.txt) remains limited to the title, abstract, and 36 deposited references. The title frames the study as a conceptual replication and the abstract reports a randomized trial evaluating mixed-reality simulation with additional coaching supports on preservice teachers' implementation of a system of least prompts (SLP). Under the codebook's description rule, this intervention and outcome uniquely bind among the 36 deposited references to bibr36 (Vince Garland, Holden, & Garland, 2016 print / 2015 online, 10.1177/0888406415600769, 'Individualized clinical coaching in the TLE TeachLivE lab: Enhancing fidelity of implementation of system of least prompts among novice teachers of students with autism'). Verified primary metadata and abstract (02_vince_metadata.body) confirm that bibr36 (published online August 18, 2015 and in print February 2016 under the exact DOI of shipped row 145) evaluated individualized clinical coaching in TLE TeachLivE mixed-reality simulation with six novice educators and found high SLP fidelity gains. Other cited simulation and feedback references (bibr2, bibr11, bibr13, bibr14, bibr16, bibr21, bibr29, bibr30, bibr33, bibr34) address comprehension, bullying, vocabulary, opportunities to respond, praise, or general simulator reviews rather than coached SLP implementation. Because bibr36 is already represented by shipped row 145, target_index 0 is not a missing row (shipped_right), while preserving that the current text is abstract-only with no body citations or requested outcome.
